author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Cyprus-based Energy Holdings has agreed to acquire deepwater drilling contractor Ventura Offshore in a share transaction that values the combined group at about $1 billion. Ventura shareholders would receive 605 million newly issued Energy Holdings shares, tying their return to the future performance of the merged offshore-drilling business.

The companies say the combination is intended to create a larger, more profitable operator with stronger cash generation and more capacity for growth and shareholder returns. The transaction brings together Energy Holdings’ capital base with Ventura’s drilling operations at a time when high oil prices and constrained offshore capacity are reshaping investment decisions across the energy-services sector.

The combined company is also considering a dual listing in the United States, which could broaden access to investors and improve trading liquidity. No U.S. listing has been finalized. The roughly $1 billion pro forma equity value is based on Energy Holdings’ latest closing price and the maximum number of shares contemplated in the deal, so it is a transaction benchmark rather than a live valuation guarantee.
dek: The stock transaction would create a larger deepwater drilling group and could be followed by a U.S. dual listing.
headline: Energy Holdings to buy Ventura Offshore in $1 billion combination
